To find ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{{e}^{x+2y}}) \\  & =-\frac{2}{{e}^{x+2y}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{2}{{e}^{x+2y}}) \\  & =-\frac{2}{{e}^{x+2y}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y)+{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =-\frac{2}{{e}^{x+2y}}-\frac{2}{{e}^{x+2y}} \\  & =-\frac{4}{{e}^{x+2y}}.\end{aligned}
$$
